note: Topic queue for the twice-weekly blog cadence. The publishing routine picks the first topic whose slug is not already in blog-posts.json, writes a full post from the brief, and ships it. Add more topics to the end of the list to extend the cadence; edit freely.

topics.title: CIS Controls IG1: The Starter Set Every Small Team Can Actually Do
topics.brief: Explain CIS Controls Implementation Group 1 as the realistic starting baseline for a small or resource-constrained team: what IG1 covers, why it maps to the most common attacks, and how to work through it without a big budget.

topics.title: From Security Analyst to Security Engineer: Making the Jump
topics.brief: A practical path for a SOC or security analyst who wants to move into a security engineering role: the skills to build (automation, cloud, code), how to get reps, and how to show the work.

topics.title: IAM vs PAM vs CIEM: Sorting Out the Identity Acronyms
topics.brief: Distinguish identity and access management, privileged access management, and cloud infrastructure entitlement management: what each governs, where they overlap, and when you need each.

topics.title: SOC 2 Readiness in Plain English
topics.brief: Demystify what getting SOC 2 ready actually involves: the Trust Services Criteria, the difference between Type I and Type II, evidence collection, and how it overlaps with other frameworks so you do the work once.

topics.title: Your First 90 Days as a Security Leader
topics.brief: A grounded first-90-days plan for a new security manager or CISO: assess the team and program, find the single points of failure, set priorities, and produce early evidence for leadership.

topics.title: Encryption at Rest vs In Transit, and Why Key Management Is the Hard Part
topics.brief: Explain encryption at rest versus in transit in plain terms, why both matter, and why key management (rotation, access, custody) is where most of the real risk and effort lives.

topics.title: DevSecOps Quick Wins Engineers Will Actually Accept
topics.brief: The highest-leverage, lowest-friction ways to add security to a software pipeline (dependency and secret scanning, pipeline hardening) and how to introduce them without slowing engineers down.

topics.title: A Sane Way to Study for the CISSP
topics.brief: A realistic CISSP study approach that respects a working professional's time: how to think in the exam's mindset, what to prioritize across the eight domains, and how to practice without burning out.

topics.title: CVSS, EPSS, and KEV: Prioritizing Patches That Matter
topics.brief: Explain how CVSS severity, EPSS exploit-likelihood, and the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog work together to prioritize patching, instead of chasing every high-severity finding.

topics.title: CMMC and NIST 800-171 for Defense Manufacturers
topics.brief: Explain what CMMC and NIST SP 800-171 require of defense-industrial-base contractors, how the levels and CUI fit together, and where to start on readiness.

topics.title: Cybersecurity Portfolio Projects That Actually Land Jobs
topics.brief: Concrete portfolio project ideas that demonstrate real security skill (a home lab, an automation, a detection, a written analysis) and how to present them so hiring managers notice.

topics.title: Phishing, MFA Fatigue, and Phishing-Resistant Authentication
topics.brief: Explain why not all MFA is equal: how attackers defeat push-based MFA with fatigue and proxy phishing, and how phishing-resistant methods (FIDO2, passkeys) close the gap.

topics.title: In the Cloud, Identity Is the Perimeter
topics.brief: Explain why identity, not the network edge, is the real perimeter in cloud environments, and the controls that follow (least privilege, conditional access, privileged access management, logging).

topics.title: Which Cloud Security Certification Should You Pursue?
topics.brief: Help a learner choose a cloud security certification path (provider certs vs vendor-neutral), matched to their goals and current level, with honest tradeoffs.

topics.title: SBOMs and Software Supply-Chain Security, Explained
topics.brief: Explain what a software bill of materials is, why supply-chain attacks made it matter, and how SBOMs, dependency scanning, and provenance fit into a real defense.

topics.title: How to Run an Incident Tabletop That Actually Helps
topics.brief: A practical guide to running a security tabletop exercise that surfaces real gaps: choosing a scenario, timed injects, who to include, and turning findings into fixes.

topics.title: What Cybersecurity Interviews Are Really Testing
topics.brief: Decode what security interviews actually assess beyond trivia: judgment, communication, and how you reason about risk, with how to prepare for each.

topics.title: EDR vs Antivirus: What Actually Changed
topics.brief: Explain how endpoint detection and response differs from traditional signature-based antivirus, what EDR adds (behavioral detection, response, telemetry), and where XDR extends it.
